newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan ends controls on foreign currency transfers.
newsitem.headline: Jordan ends controls on foreign currency transfers.

text.p: Jordan's central bank announced Sunday that it had lifted all controls on foreign currency transfers to boost foreign investments and enhance confidence in the local currency.
Jordan Central Bank Governor Ziyad Fariz said the move by the bank's board was a further step toward liberalisation of the financial sector.
He said it did away with all restrictions on amounts of foreign currency that Jordanians and local corporations can transfer or invest abroad.
"There are no longer any foreign exchange controls whatsoever, (there is) free movement of capital," Fariz said in an interview.
Free movement of capital was previously restricted to expatriate Jordanians who held non-resident foreign currency accounts and foreigners bringing in foreign currency.

"Foreign and local investors now have full freedom to get their money in and out in any currency without any restrictions. This assures them that when they bring their money to Jordan they can also take it back," Mifleh Aqel, regional manager at Jordan's leading Arab Bank, said.
Central Bank officials expect the move to further bolster the dinar, which has since 1995 been fixed at 0.709 to the dollar, by raising confidence in the financial system and hampering any outflows.
"The dinar has now become fully convertible," said another Central Bank official, adding that it would remain pegged to the same dollar value.
